name: Glycol distearate
description: Glycol distearate (CAS 627-83-8 ), also known as EGDS or ethylene glycol distearate, is a waxy ester used across personal care, coatings, and textile industries. It functions primarily as an opacifier, pearlizing agent, and rheology modifier in both aqueous and emulsion-based systems. In shampoos, conditioners, and body washes, EGDS produces the characteristic pearlescent appearance consumers associate with premium formulations, while simultaneously adjusting viscosity. Textile and fiber processing operations use it as a lubricant and surface modifier. This chemical helps to reduce friction during yarn manufacturing and fabric finishing. In coatings and emulsion systems, it acts as a co-emulsifier and consistency factor, helping stabilize formulations and control flow behavior. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to modify surface wetting and improve substrate compatibility in wax-based or fatty acid systems. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for industrial chemical formulators. Glycol distearate is supplied as white to off-white flakes or pastilles, the standard commercial form for handling and dosing in industrial and cosmetic manufacturing. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications. Cosmetic grades typically meeting purity requirements aligned with major pharmacopoeial and industry standards such as USP , BP , EP , or Ph.Eur. depending on the specific regional regulatory requirements. Drum and bulk bag packaging are common for industrial volumes, with smaller quantities available for formulation and QA sampling.
